title: Causative form (〜させる / 〜せる) "make / let someone do"
meaning: Someone makes or allows another person to do something.
simpleExplanation: The causative says that someone makes or lets another person do something: 食べる (eat) → 食べさせる (make/let someone eat). Whether it means "make" or "let" depends on the situation: a mother making a child eat vegetables is "make"; a parent allowing a child to play is "let". The person who is made to act takes に with transitive verbs (子供に野菜を食べさせる) and を with intransitive verbs (子供を学校へ行かせる).
whenUsed: Used by parents, teachers, bosses and organisations talking about what they have people do (学生に作文を書かせる). With 〜てください / 〜ていただけませんか it becomes the standard polite way to ask permission for yourself: 休ませてください (please let me rest). With 〜てあげる / 〜てくれる it leans toward "let".
formation: Group 1: ない-stem + せる: 書く→書かせる, 行く→行かせる, 待つ→待たせる, 飲む→飲ませる
Group 2: ない-stem + させる: 食べる→食べさせる, 見る→見させる
Group 3: する→させる, 来る→来させる (こさせる)
Causee (person made to act): に with a transitive verb, を with an intransitive verb
Conjugates as Group 2: 行かせます / 行かせない / 行かせた / 行かせて

diagram.root: 書く / 食べる / する / 来る

examples.ja: 母は私に部屋を掃除させました。
examples.reading: はは は わたしに へやを そうじさせました。
examples.en: My mother made me clean the room.
examples.note: Transitive verb 掃除する: the causee 私 takes に.

examples.ja: 先生は学生を立たせた。
examples.reading: せんせいは がくせいを たたせた。
examples.en: The teacher made the students stand.
examples.note: Intransitive verb 立つ: the causee 学生 takes を.

examples.ja: 子供に好きなことをさせてあげたい。
examples.reading: こどもに すきな ことを させてあげたい。
examples.en: I want to let my child do what he likes.
examples.note: させてあげる: the "let" reading.

examples.ja: 先生は学生に毎日日記を書かせています。
examples.reading: せんせいは がくせいに まいにち にっきを かかせています。
examples.en: The teacher has the students write a diary every day.
examples.note: Group 1: 書く → 書かせる. The students (causee) take に because 書く is transitive.

examples.ja: 妻を心配させたくないので、病気のことは言わなかった。
examples.reading: つまを しんぱいさせたくないので、びょうきのことは いわなかった。
examples.en: I didn't want to worry my wife, so I didn't tell her about the illness.
examples.note: Causatives of emotion verbs (心配させる, 笑わせる, 泣かせる, 喜ばせる) take を on the person.

similarGrammar.difference: The causative + てください asks permission for yourself: "please let me…". This lesson is the base form.
Told from the other side: the person forced becomes the subject (私は母に野菜を食べさせられた).
Passive = something is done to the subject; causative = the subject makes someone else act. Do not mix the endings れる and せる.

commonMistakes.wrong: 母は私を野菜を食べさせた。
commonMistakes.right: 母は私に野菜を食べさせた。
commonMistakes.why: With a transitive verb there is already an object with を (野菜を), so the causee must take に. Two を in one clause is not allowed.

commonMistakes.wrong: 先生は学生に立たせた。
commonMistakes.right: 先生は学生を立たせた。
commonMistakes.why: 立つ is intransitive, so the causee takes を.

commonMistakes.wrong: 子供を病院へ行かさせた。
commonMistakes.right: 子供を病院へ行かせた。
commonMistakes.why: Group 1 verbs take せる, not させる. 行かさせる (さ入れ) is a common slip that the exam counts as wrong.

usageNotes: The causative is used downward (parent → child, boss → staff). For asking a superior to do something you use requests (〜ていただけませんか), never the causative.
"Let" is often made explicit with あげる / くれる / もらう: 好きなだけ遊ばせてあげた (I let him play as much as he liked), 使わせてもらった (I was allowed to use it).
Emotion verbs are very common in the causative: 笑わせる (make laugh), 泣かせる (make cry), 驚かせる (surprise), 安心させる (reassure).
jlptTips: Look at the particle on the person before the blank: に + object + を points to the causative of a transitive verb; person + を with a motion verb points to the causative of an intransitive verb.
Distractors often include さ入れ forms like 行かさせる or 読まさせる. For Group 1 verbs the correct causative is ない-stem + せる (行かせる, 読ませる).
